intro.title: OAuth2 PKCE Flow in a SPA
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React single-page application (SPA) that securely logs in a user using the OAuth2 Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) flow. You will learn the core concept of generating and exchanging cryptographic codes to protect against authorization code interception attacks. The main technologies involved are React hooks for state management, the Web Crypto API for generating code verifiers and challenges, and the browser's fetch API to communicate with an OAuth2 authorization server. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a secure, standards-based authentication flow in a client-side JavaScript application.
intro.usecase: The OAuth2 PKCE flow is essential for securing single-page applications (SPAs) that integrate with third-party services like Google, GitHub, or Microsoft. Developers implement this pattern when building dashboards that display user data from external APIs, such as fitness apps showing Strava activities or project management tools syncing with Google Calendar. This security flow appears in login modals where users authenticate via "Sign in with Google" buttons, ensuring tokens aren't exposed in browser history. Every time you use a web app that accesses your Spotify playlists or Dropbox files without storing passwords, PKCE is working behind the scenes to protect your credentials.
